# Signatories

## Project team

**Aditya Bansal** (GitHub [\@adit-0132](https://github.com/adit-0132)), GSoC 2026 contributor on rdlocal, co-mentored by Heather Turner and Elio Campitelli. I'm a listed author of rdlocal, and babelrd will build on the parts I wrote, all merged upstream:

- [#35](https://github.com/eliocamp/rdlocal/pull/35): the read-time runtime that fills `{ISEXPR_n}` placeholders with live values

## Consulted

It started as my own issue for the R Project Sprint 2026 ([sprint #10](https://github.com/r-devel/r-project-sprint-2026/issues/10)): plug in your own API key, get a machine draft of a module. Paola Corrales replied:

> "Having translated only one yaml, I think it would be great to provide a way to get a machine translation as a starting point. [...] I don't think we should encourage individual users to use the package to translate documentation over and over again. This would be a waste of resources, and we'd lose the community aspect of what we do."

That reshaped the design. A translation team uses its own key to draft one module, reviews it, and then everyone installs that same module.
